title: NExT-GPT: Any-to-Any Multimodal LLM
grouping: One row per modality (Text, Image, Audio, Video, and a dashed 'More modalities' row), each labelled in plain serif at the far left, and the row colour carried through the whole row: pink for image, green for audio, purple for video, blue for text. All rows converge on one tall orange LLM block in the centre and fan out again on the right in mirror order (output projection, diffusion decoder, output icon). Along the bottom a ruler-like line with vertical tick marks splits the width into five labelled stages (input encoding, alignment, LLM understanding, alignment, output generation), so columns are grouped without any containers.
shapes_depth: Flat rounded rectangles with no shadows. Encoders and diffusion decoders are solid modality-coloured blocks with white text; input and output projections are white boxes with only a thin outline in the row colour. Inputs and outputs are flat outline icons (a document page, an image frame, a waveform, a film strip) rather than real data. Arrows are curved, coloured by row, converging into the LLM's left edge and diverging from its right; the text row bypasses all modules with long blue curves over the top. Dashed grey curves and an ellipsis stand for further modalities.
proposed_highlight: Trainable versus frozen is the emphasis: every projection (the paper's trained part) carries a small flame icon and is drawn as a hollow outlined box, while encoders, decoders and the LLM carry a snowflake and are solid fills. No extra colour or container marks 'ours'.
lesson: Frozen and trainable parts differ in fill as well as icon: frozen encoders, decoders and LLM are solid colour blocks with a snowflake, trained projections are white boxes with only a coloured outline and a flame, so the few trained parts read as light gaps in the pipeline.
notes: Mirror-symmetric input/output sides around a central LLM make the any-to-any idea visible at a glance. Venue and year from the PDF footer (Proceedings of ICML 2024).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: one row per modality on the left converges on a single tall LLM block in the centre and fans back out into mirrored per-modality output rows on the right

relations.form: curved coloured arrows from the Text icon and each input projection bend into the left side of the one LLM block that spans the image, audio and video rows

Text, Image, Audio, Video and a dashed 'More modalities' row are stacked lanes labelled at the far left, each repeating icon - encoder - input projection on the left and output projection - diffusion - icon on the right
left to right across five columns named by a tick-marked ruler along the bottom: input encoding, LLM-centric alignment, LLM understanding, instruction-following alignment, output generation
the LLM is one block spanning all modality rows in the centre column, the only module not repeated per row

channels.colour: colour = modality (pink image, green audio, purple video, blue text) on icons, boxes and arrows; the LLM's orange is outside the modality palette; output-side colours shift to a different hue (red/teal) from the input side for the same modality
channels.shape: flat outline icons = data, rounded boxes = modules; solid fill = frozen module, white fill with coloured outline = trainable projection (also marked by flame vs snowflake glyphs, so trainability is carried twice)
channels.line: solid coloured arrows = existing modality paths, dashed grey arrows = further modalities that could be added
channels.frame: no frames; the stage columns are marked only by the bottom ruler

quality.strengths: The any-to-any idea is visible as geometry: modality lanes converge on one central LLM and diverge symmetrically; the flame/snowflake plus hollow/solid fill make the few trained projections stand out; data are drawn as modality icons on both ends.
quality.weaknesses: Trainability is coded on two channels (fill and glyph) while the same-modality colour changes hue between input and output side (pink image in, red image out); the long curved Text arrows arc over the whole figure; the white-text-on-pastel labels of frozen boxes are low contrast.

insights.structure: One row per modality (Text, Image, Audio, Video, dashed 'More modalities') labelled at the far left, converging on one tall orange LLM block in the centre and mirrored on the right (output projection, diffusion decoder, output icon); a tick-marked ruler along the bottom names five column stages.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are flat outline icons (document, picture frame, waveform, film strip) coloured per modality; modules are rounded boxes, encoders and diffusion decoders solid modality-coloured fills, projections white with a coloured outline.
insights.emphasis: Trainable projections carry a flame icon and hollow outlined boxes while frozen encoders, decoders and the LLM carry a snowflake and solid fills, so the few trained parts read as light gaps.
insights.flow: Left to right: coloured curves converge into the LLM's left edge and fan out from its right; the text row bypasses all modules with long blue curves arching over the top; a dashed grey curve and ellipsis stand for further modalities.
insights.avoid: White text on pale pastel encoder/decoder fills (Image Encoder, Audio Diffusion) has low contrast and is hard to read.

arrangement.units: unframed rows per modality (row colour carried by arrows and boxes) crossed by five columns marked only by a bottom ruler with tick marks and stage labels; no enclosures
arrangement.inputs_as: modality icons with plain row labels at the far left
arrangement.shared: the single LLM block spans all rows in the centre column
